question.text: A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> block moving at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>ms</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> compresses a spring through a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> when its speed is halved. The spring constant of the spring will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Nm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>

solution.text:
Given: Mass of the block m=500 g, initial velocity of the block u=12 m s-1, and final velocity of the block v=u2=6 m s-1.

As non-conservative forces are not acting on the system we can conserve energy.

Thus, loss in kinetic energy of block = Gain in potential energy of spring

12mu2-12mv2=12kx2

12×0.5×122-12×0.5×62=12k×0.32

k=600 N m-1
